output.title: Spot duplicate emails before they become cleanup work
output.body:
If you run a small business, duplicate emails are not really a technical question. They are a workflow question: do duplicates reach you before you act on them?

Start with three recent examples from your own inbox or CRM. For each one, note where it came from: the same contact synced twice, the same person sending again, or you copying a thread into another tool. Then mark which duplicates must be caught before action and which can be cleaned up later. An invoice or payment request belongs in the first group; a newsletter usually does not. Human approval stays in place for anything involving money or other high-risk decisions.

One practical next step: run a one-week manual test. Route suspicious duplicates to one folder and review them by hand. Count only the repeats, the false positives, and the time your own review takes. If the pattern is messy, that is useful too; it means the next step is a clearer definition of “duplicate,” not a bigger tool. Small problem, small test, no drama.
